scenarios.name: Checkout Regression
scenarios.description: Checkout form rendering regresses after a product is added to the cart while homepage, catalog, product detail, and basic cart access remain healthy.
scenarios.target_domain: Checkout page and checkout frontend flow
defect_behavior: After a product is added to the cart, the checkout form no longer renders the required checkout fields or actions.
Homepage, product listing, and basic cart access should remain unaffected.
A deterministic UI-level break is preferred over a crash or timing-sensitive service failure.
notes: Validated against the full 50-test Playwright suite: 4 failed, 46 passed.
Validated external scenario commit e5234240 against baseline commit 5096a85b.
Renaming only one label may make the signal too narrow.
Service crashes may broaden the signal through HTTP 500s or slow recovery.

scenarios.name: Cart Regression
scenarios.description: Adding a product to the cart fails deterministically, creating a cart-centered signal that also affects checkout and order flows dependent on cart state.
defect_behavior: Adding a product to the cart fails deterministically.
The preferred implementation is for AddItem to return a service error instead of storing the item.
Silent no-op behavior should be avoided because generic cart text assertions may still pass on an empty-cart page.
notes: Validated against the full 50-test Playwright suite: 5 failed, 45 passed.
Validated external scenario commit f7bac607 against baseline commit 5096a85b.
Only one direct cart assertion failed; several expected cart tests remained green, which indicates those tests are broad/soft and should not be treated as validated detecting tests.
A silent cart-state drop may not be detected by tests that only assert generic cart text.
A service error gives a clearer detection signal but may create frontend error-page assertions in multiple tests.
Checkout and order flows are expected to fail because they depend on cart state.

scenarios.name: Product Detail Regression
scenarios.description: Product detail lookup for valid product IDs fails or returns unusable data while homepage product listing remains intact.
scenarios.target_domain: Product catalog service and product detail pages
defect_behavior: Product detail lookup for valid product IDs fails or returns unusable product data.
Homepage product listing should remain intact.
The preferred implementation is to break GetProduct while leaving ListProducts healthy.
notes: Breaking product data globally may also break homepage tests and make the scenario too broad.
Changing only product template text may create a frontend-only scenario rather than a product catalog scenario.
The cleanest signal is a deterministic GetProduct regression with product listing preserved.

scenarios.name: Payment Regression
scenarios.description: Valid Visa or Mastercard payments are rejected while cart, checkout form rendering, shipping quote, and product browsing remain healthy.
defect_behavior: Valid Visa or Mastercard payments are rejected.
Cart, checkout form rendering, shipping quote, and product browsing should remain healthy.
The preferred implementation is to reject otherwise valid cards after normal validation in charge.js.
notes: order-form-requires-payment-data is provisional until baseline behavior and final assertions are confirmed.
This scenario intentionally has a narrow signal and depends heavily on order-complete-happy-path.
Payment validation has date-sensitive logic, so tests should avoid relying on expiration edge cases.
